text:
hannah: FYI — Aurora Health asked for a presales packet: EU + UK + Canada residency, full sub-processor manifest, SCC/adequacy note, and a per-token egress delta. Can we assemble a concise SOW checklist?
raj: do they insist on zero-control-plane egress (i.e., private deploy) or will pinned hosted suffice?
marta: they prefer hosted pinning to go live quickly but asked for an option to avoid any control-plane crossing. BYOK required and explicit no-US-data-plane.
owen: operational note: data plane can be pinned to europe-west1 (EU), europe-west2 (UK), ca-central1; control-plane orchestration currently may route via us-east1 unless Private is chosen. Call that out in Qs.
raj: subprocessors touching in-region data plane: GCP (compute+storage), Fastly (edge cache), optional: HashiCorp Vault for BYOK. We use Datadog for metrics (no PII persisted).
marta: I'll pull the attestation pack and subproc CSV (name, country, transfer_yes_no, cert_url). ETA EOD.
hannah: egress delta — what conservative multipliers should I quote for pricing? They want per-token delta for CA + EU + UK.
lucy: ballpark estimates: ca-central1 +19%, europe-west1 +11%, europe-west2 +10% (mark as estimates). Dedicated reduces the per-token delta but adds a monthly reservation.
raj: pasteable SOW snippet we usually send:
```
residency_policy:
  allowed_regions: [europe-west1, europe-west2, ca-central1]
  data_plane: pinned
  control_plane: hosted(us-east1) # Private deployment available to eliminate control-plane egress
  kms: BYOK_supported
  egress_estimate: { ca-central1: 1.19, europe-west1: 1.11, europe-west2: 1.10 }
```
infra-bot: Provisioning alert: pinned-dataplane template validated for ca-central1 + europe-west1 (job=120334) :white_check_mark:
marta: Security Q guidance for questionnaires: Q: "Do you transfer data outside customer region?" Answer: "Data plane is pinned to customer-selected regions. Control-plane orchestration metadata may traverse other regions; Private deployment removes cross-region control-plane flows. See attached SCC annex and attestation."
hannah: Customer also asked if we can run a 1% EU+UK+CA canary for 48h to validate latency and token throughput. Any objections?
owen: Canary is fine on hosted pinned; recommend dedicated if they need guaranteed tail latency under load. No infra blocker for 48h 1% canary.
lucy: I'll draft the pricing delta + high-level dedicated vs hosted lines and drop into the deal room.
marta: uploading CSV + attestation links now: https://redwood.example.com/attestations/aurora-subprocs.csv and https://redwood.example.com/security/scc-2025.pdf
hannah: Perfect — I'll assemble the SOW and security response and send to the customer. Thanks all :thumbsup:
